When did this symbol "star of david" become the exclusive property of the religion? Does this mean muslims own the moon?
Are all 6 point stars automatically have Jewish undertones?

It isn't. It appears in Christian, Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, and even Masonic art. It appears on Masonic rings as the 'seal of Solomon', though that seal is supposed to be an interwoven line star. You can see it on some of the Pope's mitres--which often makes it the subject of conspiracy BS. It also appears in Pennsylvania Dutch hex signs. The swastika is also not exclusively a Nazi symbol. It appears in Buddhist, Christian, Hindu, and native American art. There's even an ancient Jewish form of it and a Hindu form that puts it in the middle of a Solomon seal. Before WWII, it was generally adopted as a symbol of good fortune, as it tends to be associated with in Asian culture, and was used for sports teams and appeared as decoration on a lot of architecture right here in the US. The use of the lunar crescent and star symbol in middle-east symbolism predates Islam by several thousand years, going back to the ancient Sumerians as symbolic of the gods Nanna and Inanna, surrounded by sun disk representing the god Utu.

It's how we use symbols in recent history that determines their contemporary cultural significance. The star of David is more than just a religious symbol because Nazi's forced Jews to wear it on clothing to visibly mark them as second-class citizens and make them easily spotted and singled-out in a crowd. It was then put on prison clothing and became a symbol of the Holocaust. Now it appears on the national flag of Israel. The swastika is more than just a religious symbol because the Nazi use of it tainted it by association with their actions in recent history. Many Buddhist and Hindu uses of it have stopped because of this association. The crescent star came into more recent use on the flag of the Ottoman Empire in the 19th century, became associated with Islam through the former Ottoman states specifically in the 1950s, and was adopted by Islamist movements as a symbol of Islamic nationalism in the mid 1970s. It was never really a religious symbol--it's not part of Islam--but rather a recently adopted standard of a nationalist (some might say imperialist...) movement.
